name: Epic trailer-style hybrid drum built from a four-layer synth hit (pitched additive and FM oscillators with very fast exponential pitch drops, e.g. +5 and +29 semitones, plus filtered white and pink noise bursts with overload, tube drive, MS-20-style low-pass and a high-pass) layered with any three acoustic drum samples including bleed/ambient mics, then glued with a scooped EQ, sub trim, multiband compression and gentle upward (OTT-style) compression
goal: Make big hybrid drums from tools you already have. Synth drum (one patch, four channels): (1) a simple additive/harmonic oscillator, stereo, with a pitch envelope dropping from about 5 semitones up, plus white noise through a low-pass whose cutoff envelope closes extremely fast with a strong exponential curve (a pitched, roto-tom-like burst); (2) pink noise through an aggressive low-pass with the same envelope, then a second overloaded filter that also takes channel 1's signal for grit; (3) an FM (or simple triangle/square) oscillator with a very fast pitch drop into tube distortion, an MS-20-style low-pass and a high-pass to remove rumble; (4) another additive high-content oscillator whose pitch drop starts about 29 semitones up, giving parallel pitch drops with channel 1. Key: very fast, strongly curved envelopes that hit hard and decay to nothing; play lower or higher on the keyboard for pitch, or several notes for a flam/ensemble. Global: two EQs, compression and reverb. Acoustic layer: any three acoustic drum samples, mixed with room/bleed mics (snare, hats, toms, ambience) so the kick is not dead. Process the combined layers: heavily scooped EQ for a trailer sound, trim the very lowest subs, per-layer EQ (less top on acoustic), multiband compression on the low end letting transients through, and optionally OTT-style compression at low depth with more upward than downward. Render the acoustic element, set its notes to the sample's root pitch and add the same fast envelope in the sampler; add velocity tracking for dynamics.

source.title: How to Make Your Own Epic Hybrid Drums WITHOUT Buying New Sounds (Tutorial)

prerequisites: A synth with several oscillators, noise sources, pitch and filter envelopes with adjustable curve, distortion and filters
Any acoustic drum samples (ideally with room/bleed mics)
EQ, multiband compressor, optional OTT-style upward/downward compressor, reverb

inputs.name: acoustic_samples
inputs.description: Three acoustic drum layers (kick/low drum, snare, ambience)

inputs.name: pitch_range
inputs.description: Keyboard range for the synth layer's pitch

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
The speaker's synth and FL Studio effects are mapped to generic oscillators, noise, filters, tube drive and multiband compression; no presets or library samples are copied.
The envelope curve is the key element: linear decays sound wrong; use fast, strongly exponential decays on pitch, filter and amp.
Extreme multiband presets need EQ afterwards; keep OTT-style depth low.
For Matt's ambient/cinematic tracks these hits suit early, steady pulses and impacts; keep them out of the way of the sub.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Channel 1: additive/harmonic oscillator, stereo, with a pitch envelope dropping from about +5 semitones; fast exponential amp envelope.
Channel 2: white noise into a low-pass whose cutoff envelope closes extremely fast with a strong curve.
Channel 3: pink noise into an aggressive low-pass using the same envelope, then a second overloaded filter that also receives channel 1.
Channel 3: FM (or triangle/square) oscillator with a very fast pitch drop into tube distortion, an MS-20-style low-pass, then a high-pass to cut rumble.
Channel 4: a second additive high-content oscillator whose pitch drop starts about +29 semitones; play with channel 1 for parallel pitch drops.
steps.expect: A bright pitched attack on top.

steps.action: Add global EQ (two), compression and reverb; compare a less-curved envelope to confirm the strong curve is needed.
steps.expect: A finished synth drum that plays pitch by key and flams with multiple notes.

steps.action: Layer three acoustic drum samples, bringing up bleed/ambient mics (snare, hats, toms, room) so the low drum has life.
steps.expect: An acoustic layer with air and character.

steps.action: On the combined layers: heavily scooped EQ, trim the very lowest subs, per-layer EQ (e.g. less top on the acoustic), multiband compression on the low band letting transients through.
steps.expect: Controlled rumble with clear attacks; a trailer-drum tone.

steps.action: Optionally add OTT-style compression at low depth with more upward than downward; EQ after any extreme multiband effect.
steps.expect: Denser, more aggressive hits without harshness.

steps.action: Render the acoustic element, set its notes to the sample's root pitch, apply the same fast envelope in the sampler and add velocity tracking to both layers.
steps.expect: Playable, dynamic hybrid hits ready to sequence.

verification: Each synth channel has a pitch or filter envelope with a strongly curved fast decay.
At least two layers have pitch drops starting at different intervals (+5 and +29 st).
The hybrid bus has the lowest sub trimmed and a visibly scooped mid EQ.
